simple.meaning: יָמַן (yâman) is a Hebrew action word meaning “to be right-handed or take the right-hand side.” BibleIQ anchors the English reading to this source verb before comparing its uses.
simple.biblicalBackground: This action appears 4 times in Genesis, 2 Samuel, 1 Chronicles, Ezekiel, beginning at Genesis 13:9. The surrounding contexts include kingship, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to יָמַן (H3231) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Actions in Scripture show what people do, what God does, and how covenant faithfulness or rebellion is described. BibleIQ compares the action across its occurrences.
simple.summary: יָמַן (yâman) / H3231 is traced through Genesis 13:9, 2 Samuel 14:19, 1 Chronicles 12:2, Ezekiel 21:21 with source-language evidence and verse context.

definitions.short: to be right-handed or take the right-hand side
definitions.usage: go (turn) to (on, use) the right hand.
definitions.full: to be right-handed or take the right-hand side
definitions.rootNote: a primitive root; to be (physically) right (i.e. firm); but used only as denominative from 3225 and transitive,

occurrences.englishText: Isn’t the whole land before you? Please separate yourself from me. If you go to the left hand, then I will go to the right. Or if you go to the right hand, then I will go to the left.”
The king said, “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?”
They were armed with bows, and could use both the right hand and the left in slinging stones and in shooting arrows from the bow. They were of Saul’s relatives of the tribe of Benjamin.

For the king of Babylon stood at the parting of the way, at the head of the two ways, to use divination. He shook the arrows back and forth. He consulted the teraphim.† teraphim were household idols that may have been associated with inheritance rights to the household property. He looked in the liver.
